clue.text: Singer having consecutive number ones?

indicators.note: consecutive says the two slang words follow one straight after the other

parts.note: 'number ones' is nursery slang for urinating; the first of the two consecutive ones is a pee
the second of the two consecutive number ones is a wee, another child's word for urinating

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a pop star who had a run of chart-topping hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number ones' looks like chart hits, but it is nursery slang for urinating: PEE and WEE, two in a row ('consecutive').
explanation.definitionFit: The peewee is a songbird (a name for the lapwing and for the pewee flycatcher), so it is a singer.

clue.text: Liking swan song

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: A fondness for the swan song, a final performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swan song' looks like one phrase, but it splits into a female swan and a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or fondness, a synonym.

clue.text: Sword passed on by Charlie before burial at sea

indicators.note: before puts these letters ahead of what follows

parts.note: ex means former or no longer living, gone
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A sword is handed down by Charlie before he is buried at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges BURIAL into ALIBUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Excalibur is King Arthur's legendary sword.

clue.text: Promoted unknown Lincoln marketplace

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, so in this down entry the two pieces together are read upwards

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic unknown
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: An unknown Lincoln marketplace gets promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' is the president, not the English city; 'Promoted' turns the whole pair upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is an online auction site, a virtual marketplace.

clue.text: Splendid Cheddar perhaps alongside donuts served regularly

parts.note: Cheddar Gorge is a famous limestone gorge in Somerset, England, so Cheddar is an example of a gorge

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the word donuts, as if dealt out in turn

explanation.surface: A cheese platter served with doughnuts is declared splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheddar' suggests cheese, but Cheddar Gorge is a ravine in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms meaning beautiful or magnificent.

clue.text: Previous jail sentence under twelve months

indicators.note: under places the jail sentence below the other piece in this down entry

parts.note: twelve months makes one year, so it gives one
doing time is serving a jail sentence

explanation.surface: A prison term of less than a year was imposed before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under twelve months' looks like a duration, but 'under' places TIME below ONE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, a synonym of previous.

clue.text: Unusually large theologian overwhelming for president

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are put in an unusual order
overwhelming means engulfing, so the theologian's letters surround the word for

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A huge theologian puts himself forward for president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges the letters of 'large', and DD is a Doctor of Divinity; 'for' is taken as written, not as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was the 38th President of the United States.

clue.text: How Scandi characters become sad? In a peculiar way

definitions.meaning: Odd is a common Norwegian man's name, so Scandinavian characters called Odd could become sad in an Odd way

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about why Scandinavians become gloomy, answered: strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like letters, but means people; Odd is a Norwegian forename.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddly is the adverb of odd, meaning strangely.

clue.text: One distributing Bible in company of soothsayer

indicators.note: in company of says the Bible's letters sit inside the soothsayer's

parts.note: a seer is a soothsayer
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A man hands out Bibles alongside a fortune-teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in company of' puts RV into SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A server hands out food or drink, or a tennis player puts the ball into play.

clue.text: Seize control of countryman bypassing European agreement

indicators.note: bypassing means passing around, so the countryman's letters go around the agreement

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated rural person
ja is German (and Dutch, and Scandinavian) for yes

explanation.surface: Seizing a rural man's property and ignoring an EU treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European agreement' looks like a treaty, but it is the German yes, JA.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to take over by force, especially a vehicle.

clue.text: Irish over in canteen munched fruit

indicators.note: food that is munched is chewed up, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irishman in a works canteen chomps through some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munched' scrambles IR together with the letters of CANTEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Haggard feature of Bill?

parts.note: It is also a clause added to a parliamentary bill

explanation.surface: A question about what makes someone called Bill look gaunt and worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' reads as gaunt, but it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard; 'Bill' is a draft law, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's middle name, and also the term for an amendment attached to a legislative bill.

clue.text: Temporarily stop Henry the Eighth in flagrante

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: the Eighth in says take the eighth letter of the word flagrante

explanation.surface: A command to halt Henry VIII, caught red-handed with one of his wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry the Eighth' reads as the king, but it splits: Henry is HAL, and 'the Eighth in flagrante' is that word's eighth letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to come to a stop, usually for a while, so it means pause.

clue.text: Artist first to decry reality broadcast that's typically inflated

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: first to says take only the opening letter of the word decry
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist is the first to criticise a reality TV show, a genre known for exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests television, but it rearranges REALITY into IALTYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial is a kind of car tyre, and tyres are pumped up with air.

clue.text: US novelist in good health grazed freely, drinking litres

parts.note: to be fit is to be in good health

indicators.note: drinking says the scrambled letters take in the litres abbreviation
freely says the letters are allowed to move about

explanation.surface: A healthy animal grazes at will, drinking litres of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges GRAZED, and 'drinking' slips L inside to give ZGERALD.
explanation.definitionFit: F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote The Great Gatsby.

clue.text: Old iron spike given slight wash

parts.note: a nib is a sharp point, like a spike
a lick, as in 'a lick and a promise', is a quick, cursory wash

explanation.surface: An old iron spike is given a quick clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old iron' looks like scrap metal, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick was an old name for a lofted golf club, roughly a nine iron.

clue.text: Wrap up Parisian in France with cold, heading off

parts.note: en is French for in, as a Parisian would say it
F is the international vehicle code for France

indicators.note: heading off says the word cold loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to wrap up warm in France when the cold sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the C of COLD, leaving OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold something is to wrap or envelop it, a synonym.

clue.text: Heather picks up earthy pigment, dealing with timber

indicators.note: picks up means takes on board, so the heather's letters hold the pigment

parts.note: ling is a name for common heather
umber is a natural brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather picks up a brown paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a name, but it is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering is the business of felling and preparing timber.

clue.text: Music player from Cambridge college keeps in time

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the college's letters hold the word in

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A musician from a Cambridge college keeps in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps in time' sounds like a musician staying on the beat, but 'in' is a piece of the wordplay held by the college.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, something played to make music.

clue.text: Underwear Elizabeth rejected somewhere in Latin America

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Liz is a short form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth turns down some underwear somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the short name round.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil is the largest country in South America, part of Latin America.

clue.text: Reflective type of painting by Geordie hosting is put on pedestal

indicators.note: by places one piece beside the next
reflective suggests a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an oil is a painting in oil paints

indicators.note: hosting means having as a guest, so these letters surround the word is

parts.note: a Geordie is someone from Newcastle, in the North East (NE) of England

explanation.surface: A contemplative oil painting by an artist from Newcastle is placed on a pedestal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' looks like a description of the painting, but it turns OIL to LIO.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, worship them.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow vehicle male shifted

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: shifted means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man moves a brownish-yellow vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges MALE into AMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel names a light golden-brown colour, like toffee.

clue.text: Place of security functioning beneath two businesses

indicators.note: beneath places the functioning piece below the others in this down entry
two says the abbreviation is written twice

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
something on is working

explanation.surface: A safe place lies underneath two companies working together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath' puts ON below COCO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is a silky protective case, a refuge.

clue.text: Evaluate a bearing between ships

indicators.note: between puts the bearing in the middle of the ship abbreviations

parts.note: SS stands for steamship; plural ships give SS twice
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A navigator assesses a bearing between two vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ships' needs two SS abbreviations, one on each side of E.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge or appraise something.

clue.text: Western trainer prioritising leg

indicators.note: prioritising puts the leg first, ahead of the trainer

parts.note: a stage is a leg of a journey
a coach is a sports trainer

explanation.surface: A trainer from the West who puts leg exercises first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' looks like an adjective, but it is a film genre: the classic John Ford Western.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagecoach (1939) is a celebrated John Ford film, a Western.

clue.text: That is blocking middle of viaduct for so long

indicators.note: blocking means obstructing, so the abbreviation sits in the middle of the central letters
middle of says take the central letters of the word viaduct

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Something is blocking the centre of a viaduct, which has been the case for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' reads as duration, but it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, like the casual farewell 'so long'.

clue.text: Don, an English river

definitions.meaning: to don clothes is to put them on
the River ... flows through Durham and Sunderland in northeast England

explanation.surface: The Don, a river, is said to be English (though it is in Yorkshire too).
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a river (there are English and Scottish Dons), but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on clothes is to wear them; the second sense is a river in County Durham.

clue.text: Open market

explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just or above board, like an open contest; a fair is also a periodic market.

clue.text: Musical beat I verbalise partly, making comeback

indicators.note: making comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer beats out a rhythm and says words, staging a comeback in a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Perón.

clue.text: New lino's outside at number ten, being detached

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters surround the word at
new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ten is written as the figures 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: New lino laid outside the door of Number Ten, the Prime Minister's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number ten' looks like Downing Street but gives IO; 'New' rearranges LINOS with IO into ISOLION, which goes 'outside' AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is the state of being cut off or set apart, a synonym.

clue.text: More robust undergraduate stifles resistance

indicators.note: stifles means smothers, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: an undergraduate is one who studies, a studier
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A tougher student keeps down any opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdier is the comparative of sturdy, meaning stronger or more solid.

clue.text: Alarm loud and sinister? Just the opposite

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
sinister is Latin and heraldic for left, so its opposite is the other side

explanation.surface: Asks whether alarm is noisy and threatening, then says the reverse is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' reads as menacing, but it is Latin for left; 'just the opposite' turns it to the other hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden scare, and alarm is fear at sudden danger.
